title: Apollo 11: the landing day

sentences.speaker: spk_0
sentences.text: July 20, 1969. At 1:44 in the afternoon, Eastern time, the lunar module Eagle undocks from Columbia, with Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin aboard.

sentences.speaker: spk_0
sentences.text: Michael Collins stays behind, orbiting the Moon alone.

sentences.speaker: spk_0
sentences.text: At 4:05 PM, Eagle's descent engine fires for the powered descent to the surface.

sentences.speaker: spk_0
sentences.text: Minutes later, the guidance computer throws a 1202 program alarm. Mission control decides it is safe to keep going.

sentences.speaker: spk_0
sentences.text: The planned landing spot is strewn with boulders, so Armstrong takes manual control and flies on, looking for flat ground, while the fuel runs low.

sentences.speaker: spk_0
sentences.text: At 4:17 PM, Eagle touches down in the Sea of Tranquility. The Eagle has landed.

sentences.speaker: spk_0
sentences.text: That night, at 10:56 PM, Armstrong steps onto the Moon: one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind.

sentences.speaker: spk_0
sentences.text: About twenty minutes later, Aldrin joins him on the surface.
